answer: Sybil resistance comes from per-identity proof-of-work with a slashed bond: each agent generates a fresh key and grinds a nonce until hashing it with the network's cipher seed clears a difficulty target. The puzzle is memory-hard and non-batchable, so forging a thousand fake agents costs a thousand full solves, not one. Each identity also locks collateral held like timber in escrow and slashed on double-signing. Even if Sybils hide in a karst of tangled proxies, work and stake stay on the public ledger, so the attacker pays full price per fake identity.
